extracted.intended_audience: biographers, literary critics, and educated readers interested in the craft and evaluation of biography
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply critical standards for writing or judging biography (what makes a faithful, memorable, and literary life-writing). Emphasizes veracity, selection, style, method, and moral/procedural choices of the biographer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confining subject to dignity/respectability
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity and respectability have ruined alike the historian and the biographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit a life to courtly or heroic episodes (the 'proper'); include mundane, vulgar, or lowly material that shows true character. Anti-pattern: producing a sanitized, court-ridden account that obscures the real nature of the person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to tell the truth 'truly and intelligibly'
rubrics_metrics.description: The biographer's duty is 'to tell what he had to say truly and intelligibly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When delicate material is relevant, it should be reported rather than omitted to preserve historical truth. Example: Lockhart judged it right to include awkward facts when necessary; omission for reputation's sake misconceives the biographer's province.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity as the prime quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Disingenuousness is a charge that never could have occurred to Boswell, whose veracity is the prime quality that has made him immortal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and honesty in reporting facts, conversations, and documents are central. Scoring note: a work that cannot be vouched for by reliable witnesses or documentation loses essential credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of letters and private details when integral
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of the letters and of private details was an integral part of his scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private correspondence and domestic detail can illuminate character and should be used when they serve the understanding of the subject. Anti-pattern: omitting private materials that are relevant to the person's actions or public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention peculiarities because they mark character
rubrics_metrics.description: "In writing a man's life the man's peculiarities should be mentioned because they mark his character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record idiosyncrasies—small habits, speech, and eccentricities—as evidentiary markers of personality rather than embarrassments to be hidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sanitize the subject to please readers
rubrics_metrics.description: I will not ... 'cut off his claws, nor make a tiger a cat to please anyone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist pressures (moralizers, friends, reviewers) urging mitigation of asperities or excision of faults. Authentic portrayal may offend contemporary sensibilities but serves posterity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and external corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authenticity is of the utmost consequence"; Boswell dedicated works to persons who could vouch for their truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use endorsements, witnesses, manuscript checks, and knowledgeable correspondents to validate claims. Example: dedicating or sending manuscripts to reliable contemporaries who can attest to accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the characteristical and typical; group and dramatize
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the art of Boswell to select 'the characteristical,' and the typical, to group and to dramatize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simple garrulous accumulation; choose incidents and quotations that are characteristic and arrange them for dramatic and interpretive effect. Anti-pattern: 'tourist' note-books that record everything without selection or art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptive observation ('the seeing eye') combined with openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness of mind will do much, but there must be the seeing eye behind it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A biographer must be both open-minded and observant—able to detect significance in small details and to sympathize without losing critical distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve conversations faithfully (but expect editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported in his short-hand, yet 'so as to keep the substance and language of discourse?' — some passages appear 'pointed and improved' in final form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to retain the substance and natural language of conversations; limited editing for clarity and effect is acceptable, but wholesale invention or distortion of quoted speech is an anti-pattern. Note: readers and critics will scrutinize how much a reporter 'Johnsonized' or altered dialogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit or disguise scandalously relevant relations
rubrics_metrics.description: A biographer that would omit or disguise the relations of Nelson to Lady Hamilton, would be justly suspected of disingenuousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report relationships and facts that materially affect understanding of deeds and reputation; concealment undermines credibility. Exception: strictly redundant or irrelevantly salacious material may be excluded if not illuminating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meticulous method and assiduity in research
rubrics_metrics.description: He knew the value of his work... 'obliged to run half over London in order to fix a date correctly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful checking of dates, sources, and statements, and persistent archival work are marks of a responsible biographer. Scoring note: sloppy chronology or avoidable factual errors are serious faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary qualities: clear, rounded, and dramatic prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all his contemporaries... no one is a greater master of a pure prose style than Boswell, and for ease of narrative, felicity of phrase, and rounded diction he is incomparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond accuracy, exemplary biography should be written with stylistic skill—ease of narrative, apt phrasing, and the power to render scenes vividly. Anti-pattern: dull, decorous prose that obscures human interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of travel, cosmopolitan experience, and wider reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign travel had done much... 'I am... completely a citizen of the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader cultural experience and reading enrich perspective and judgment; a biographer informed by travel and comparative observation has greater sympathy and context for the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between recording and selection (note-book vs art)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tourist puts in everything he sees... But it is the art of Boswell to select 'the characteristical'... The note-book gave them no permanence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect material thoroughly but exercise editorial selection—transform raw notes into durable, interpretive writing. Anti-pattern: publishing unselected garrulity that lacks thematic cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: A biographer may improve or refine material conscientiously
rubrics_metrics.description: The final form in which stories appear in the later book is always that of a pointed and improved nature... Boswell ... did consciously or otherwise add much to the originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some degree of shaping, point-making, and polishing of raw material is acceptable when done transparently and without inventing facts; avoid claiming direct transcripts when substantial reworking has occurred.
